title: Ex-compatriots' bar and Baron Rosencratz
summary: Resuming February 2, Butler describes musicians returned from Paris who hung out at a bar run by Baron Rosencratz and his reporter wife near Edgecombe Avenue.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: This is February 2nd, 1979, 65 Second Avenue, Jacques Butler's home. Now, you've told me that -- before we talk about your going back to Europe after World War II -- you mentioned that you worked with Art (Hodes?) and a lot of so-called Dixieland bands, but you had also told me that on occasion before, that you had used Bud Powell at one time on your bands.

Yeah, I used Bud Powell. You see, there was -- Billy Lewis and all of us, we were ex-compatriots, we had come back from Europe, so we always hung together. And there was a reporter, her name was Inez (Timmy) Cavanaugh, she married a baron whose name was Baron Rosen-cratz (phonetic). And Baron Rosencratz had very little, very sharp bar, or something, just for his pleasure, and we always hung out there because we always talking. Everyone that would come from Paris, France, places, they would find that -- because we had things in common to talk about.
This was on Edgecombe Avenue, next to a place called La Macherie.
On 47th Street, right. And so, the musicians were coming down and they were jamming and,
